title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This typescript page is evidently a draft of §8 of 'Le groupe de Brauer III' (Dix exposés, 1968). The setting is the Brauer group of a smooth projective surface X over an algebraically closed field k, with ℓ ≠ char k. The Tate twist is written [n] instead of (n).

1. Poincaré duality. The cup product H^2(X,Z_ℓ(1)) × H^2(X,Z_ℓ(1)) → H^4(X,Z_ℓ(2)) ≅ Z_ℓ is non-degenerate, indeed perfect, modulo torsion.

2. Restriction to NS. Via the Chern class map, the form restricts on NS(X)⊗Z_ℓ to the intersection form on divisors. Matsusaka's theorem says divisors numerically equivalent to zero are algebraically equivalent to zero up to torsion. So the intersection form on NS/tors is non-degenerate.

3. Rational splitting. Tensor the exact sequence (8.7), 0 → NS⊗Z_ℓ → H^2(X,Z_ℓ(1)) → T_ℓ Br(X) → 0, with Q_ℓ. Then V_ℓ Br ≅ NS_Q^⊥ inside H^2(X,Q_ℓ(1)), and the cup product restricted to this space is non-degenerate.

4. Integral question. Transport the form to T_ℓ Br. Since T_ℓ Br is torsion-free, NS⊗Z_ℓ is saturated in H^2/tors, which is unimodular. Let N = NS⊗Z_ℓ and T' = N^⊥. The image of T_ℓ Br in NS_Q^⊥ is the orthogonal projection of H^2/tors, which is T'^*. The form is Z_ℓ-valued on T'^* iff T'^* = T', i.e. iff T' is unimodular. For a primitive sublattice of a unimodular lattice, disc(T') = ±disc(N), so this holds iff disc(NS/tors) is an ℓ-adic unit. That is true for almost all ℓ, and then T_ℓ Br is self-dual.

5. Finite quotient (8.3). The Kummer sequence gives (8.8): the ℓ-part of Br'(X)/Br'(X)^0 ≅ H^2(X,μ_ℓ∞)/(maximal divisible subgroup), because Pic⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ = NS⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ is divisible. The universal-coefficient sequence (8.3) for i=3 reads 0 → H^2(Z_ℓ(1))⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ → H^2(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1)) → Tors H^3(Z_ℓ(1)) → 0. It gives (8.9): Br'/Br'^0 (ℓ-part) ≅ Tors H^3(X,Z_ℓ(1)), valid for any X.

6. The page breaks off announcing the classical duality relations, obtained from SGA4 XIX duality by passage to the limit. These are presumably the duality of Br/Br^0 with torsion of NS / H^2, as in the published text.
errors: (8.8)–(8.9) as written should be read on ℓ-primary components (ℓ ≠ p); the page leaves this implicit.
The integrality argument silently uses that NS⊗Z_ℓ is saturated in H^2/torsion (from torsion-freeness of T_ℓ). It is correct but unstated.

ideas.what: Under Poincaré duality, T_ℓ Br ⊗ Q is the orthogonal of NS in H^2(X,Q_ℓ(1)) and carries a non-degenerate form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript draft (with handwritten corrections) of a passage that appears essentially verbatim in the published 'Le groupe de Brauer III' §8. Its presence in the 'standard conjectures' dossier is mildly interesting archivally but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'Br^#(X)' is the typescript's (overstruck) Br'(X); read Br'(X).
Handwritten subscript rendered as χ in the image is ℓ throughout (Z_ℓ, Q_ℓ, T_ℓ).
'[15] [?]' is '[15] 3.' — handwritten citation, with the struck/overwritten numeral before 'D'après'.
Top-right handwritten page number reads '43' (typescript pagination); bottom-left '22' is the archive page.
The struck opening of the paragraph is 'D'après Ilxxxxx', a struck-out false start.
The SGAA reference is handwritten as 'XIX', underlined, as in the transcription.
